full_judgment: 2. The petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 932 of 1982 in the Court of Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka for declaration that the Revenue sale held on 25.9.45 is null and void and not binding upon them. Their case was that the taluk including the suit land measuring 1.42 acres originally belonged to one Radha Chand Naha and on his death his interest devolved upon his sons Govinda Charan Naha and Prasanna Kumar in equal share in ejmali. While they were owning the same Govinda Charan Naha sold his half share to the plaintiffs by registered kabala dated 15.5.43. Prosanna Kumar Naha also settled his share to the plaintiffs on receiving proper salami in January, 1944. The petitioners thus owned and possessed the entire property in Khas on the basis of purchase and lease. The petitioners in 1945 settled the land of CS plot No. 5233 with Monsur Ali who owned and possessed the same and got his name recorded in SA Khatian. The land of Monsur Ali was acquired in LA Case No. 49 of 1963-64 and compensation was prepared in the names of Nur Mohammad and Motazuddin sons of Monsur Ali who received the compensation. The Touzi, however, subsequent to the purchase by the petitioners was sold in revenue sale on 25.9.45 for arrear of Revenue and was auction purchased by one Chand Mia who without getting any physical possession of the land sold the same to Prasanna Kumar Naha on 23.4.46 who in his turn transferred his interest to one Moula Box the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite party by lease dated 9.3.1949. It is alleged that petitioners were not impleaded in the Revenue sale as parties and as such the same was not binding on him and their interest has not been affected by the Revenue sale. But the opposite parties on the strength of the alleged perpetual lease dated 9.3.49 threatened the petitioners with dispossession from the suit land on 7.3.82 resulting in filing the present suit. During pendency of the said Title Suit No. 932 of 1982 the opposite parties got delivery of possession of the suit land in pursuance of Execution Proceeding arising out of Title Suit No. 5 of 1959 although the petitioners were not made parties in their personal capacity in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 5 of 1959. In this back ground the petitioners sought amendment of the plaint by filing an application under Order 6 rule 17 read with section 151 CPC to the effect that the decree made in Title Suit No. 5 of 1959 arising out of revenue sale dated 25.9.45 was null and void. The said application was rejected by the learned Munsif on 2.1.1985 giving rise to the present Rule.
